findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile Tier-1/Tier-2 (LLM re-runs) against ADR 0054 §2's rejection of purpose-built LLM eval suites and bulk re-review sweeps — invoke ADR 0054's §2 'evals for their own purposes' carve-out (this is an instrument, not a per-change calibration), and state why the tiers are not the rejected category.
evidence: ADR 0054 §2: 'The following MUST NOT be required, planned, or commissioned … Purpose-built LLM eval suites built for a single calibration question. Bulk re-review sweeps — re-running review-plan / review-code across a corpus of tickets to observe how a candidate value would have scored.'
The plan invokes ADR 0054 as SUPPORT ('Consistent with ADR 0054') but only for Tier 0; Tier 1/2 are bulk LLM re-runs.

ADR 0054 §2 last paragraph DOES carve out 'evals used for their own purposes (prompt development, regression pinning of model behavior, capability checks)' and the existing ab_impact_model.py — a reconciliation path the plan does not invoke.
findings.finding: The plan's Tier-1 (re-run the verifier over the corpus) and Tier-2 (re-run finders over a sample) are precisely the 'purpose-built LLM eval suite' and 'bulk re-review sweep' categories that ADR 0054 §2 explicitly REJECTS, yet the plan cites ADR 0054 only as support for its offline-first/Tier-0 stance and never reconciles the LLM tiers against that rejection.
findings.location: Approach — 'Tier 1 — Pass-2 replay', 'Tier 2 — Pass-1 replay'; Invariant 3 'Offline first … Consistent with ADR 0054'
scenarios: A reviewer or the ADR-0054 author reads the epic as directly contradicting an Accepted ADR the epic itself cites, and blocks it on governance grounds.
The commissioning Tier-1/Tier-2 spend (≤$120) is exactly the 'most expensive part of a calibration' ADR 0054 warns against, absent an explicit carve-out argument.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a paragraph (and a line in the ADR this epic ships) explicitly citing ADR 0054 §2's carve-out for 'regression pinning of model behavior / capability checks', framing Tier-1/2 as building a standing instrument (not gating a single calibration value), and bounding when a Tier-1/2 run is permitted vs when Tier-0 alone suffices.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the child ordering so the budget ledger (4c80) and model-parity guard (efd4) land before the Tier-1/Tier-2 harnesses (53ab/f1d6) that depend on them, or add explicit depends_on links.
evidence: Parent 'Child decomposition': '... → Tier-1 harness (4) → Tier-2 harness (5) → budget ledger + model-parity guard + homogeneous Bedrock chain (6, 7, 8; ...)'
53ab Approach: 'All calls go through the budget ledger pre-flight (estimate = stored metrics tokens × current price × N) and record the model id per result.'
efd4 Approach: 'Build src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/parity.py and wire it into every tier' — tier1.py/tier2.py hook into parity
f1d6 Testing: 'a run is refused when the frontier model is not the Bedrock Opus id' — requires efd4's parity guard
findings.finding: Ordering violation in the child decomposition: the parent orders the tier harnesses (Tier-1 = 53ab, Tier-2 = f1d6) BEFORE the budget ledger (4c80) and model-parity guard (efd4) ('Tier-1 harness (4) → Tier-2 harness (5) → budget ledger + model-parity guard + homogeneous Bedrock chain (6, 7, 8)'), yet both tier children hard-depend on the ledger and parity guard already existing. 53ab: 'All calls go through the budget ledger pre-flight ... and record the model id per result'; f1d6: 'a run is refused when the frontier model is not the Bedrock Opus id' and 'Budget pre-flight'. A Tier-1/Tier-2 harness cannot be built or commissioned before the ledger/parity infrastructure it calls into.
scenarios: A contributor implements 53ab/f1d6 in the stated decomposition order and finds the ledger.reserve() pre-flight and parity.py guards do not yet exist, so the tier harness cannot pass its own AC (priced ledger rows, model-id refusal) until 4c80/efd4 land.
Commissioning a Tier-1 reproduction run (≤$40) before the ledger exists means the spend is untracked, violating the parent's hard-budget invariant.
findings.suggested_fix: Reorder the decomposition to place ledger + parity guard before the LLM tier harnesses, or state that 53ab/f1d6 depend_on 4c80 and efd4 and must not commission live runs before those land.

98df's promotion decision (advisory→blocking) could be read as touching a production criterion, brushing the parent's non-goal, if it is assumed to be inside this epic.

scenarios: Author runs the self-vs-self zero-diff check over all v2 sidecars and sees non-zero diffs on every pre-v5 finding, mistaking version artifacts for a harness bug or a regression signal
A Pass-3 formula change is scored over pooled cohorts, inflating or masking the true blast radius
findings.suggested_fix: Add IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION as a required corpus-manifest dimension; Tier-0 groups by version, replays each finding only against the formula that produced it, and the self-vs-self zero-diff AC is asserted per-cohort (current plan-v5 segment), matching sidecar.py's no-pool rule and ADR 0036/0054.
